Genes, Populations, & Evolution
Population of moths outside London –25 moths collected for 3 seasons and allele frequency remained the same (p=0.2, q=0.8).  Since alleles same -no evolution
explanation: This slide provides a concrete example of genetic stability in a natural population. Geneticists collected 25 moths outside London over three seasons and observed that the allele frequencies remained constant at p = 0.2 and q = 0.8. Because the allele frequencies did not change over this time period, no microevolution had occurred in the moth population.

questions.q: In the moth study outside London, why was it concluded that no evolution occurred?
opts: The allele frequencies remained constant (p=0.2, q=0.8) over the three seasons.
All moths possessed identical physical phenotypes.
The population size dropped to zero.
questions.exp: Evolution did not occur because the allele frequencies remained the same (p=0.2, q=0.8) over the three seasons, showing that microevolutionary changes were absent.
